answer: Anchor each identity to one registered domain name, a pearl on a string: the protocol checks a DNS TXT record the owner signs with the epoch nonce, so a willow-thin claim fails without the registrar's signature. One domain issues one credential; WHOIS history must show 90 days of registration, about $12 a year, so a farm cannot pre-age a hundred names overnight. A comet of nonces sweeps past each epoch, forcing re-signing; replayed records die, and two identities sharing a domain collapse to one vote with stake burned. A hundred votes means a hundred domains; an honest agent pays once.
